subject.title: fix(imessage): repair DM sender fallback before pairing

question: For non-group, not-from-me iMessage payloads where sender normalizes to destination_caller_id but chat_identifier or participants indicate a different peer, should OpenClaw repair only canonical-normalization-confident peers and drop otherwise before access control?
rationale: The sender rewrite happens before authorization and delivery routing, so automation cannot choose the security boundary for ambiguous or unrepairable identity payloads.

options.title: Repair Confidently, Drop Otherwise
options.body: Require canonical iMessage normalization for sender, destination, and peer candidates, and fail closed when the peer cannot be recovered confidently before access control.

options.title: Repair Only The Confident Case
options.body: Limit this PR to canonical-normalized confident repair and leave a separate follow-up for fail-closed handling of unrepairable payloads.

options.title: Pause This Branch
options.body: Keep the branch draft or close it if the author's remaining failures point to a different iMessage root cause.

recommendation.title: Repair Confidently, Drop Otherwise
recommendation.body: Require canonical iMessage normalization for sender, destination, and peer candidates, and fail closed when the peer cannot be recovered confidently before access control.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the merged anchorless iMessage watch-payload repair in the same module and already requested live proof on this PR.
